subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw make unset Docker sandbox containers default to a 1024 PID cap, and what explicit opt-out or migration contract should ship with that change?
rationale: This is a security hardening tradeoff that changes existing runtime defaults and can break process-heavy sandbox or browser workloads, so code inspection cannot safely choose the default and compatibility contract alone.

options.title: Approve capped default with opt-out
options.body: Keep the 1024 default only if the PR also documents and validates an explicit way to preserve Docker-default behavior, adds tests, and includes real Docker proof.

options.title: Keep Docker default for now
options.body: Do not merge the fallback until maintainers choose a broader resource-limit policy or a default-off hardening mode.

options.title: Choose a different resource policy
options.body: Replace the one-line PID fallback with a maintainer-approved policy covering PID, memory, CPU, browser workload, and upgrade behavior together.

recommendation.title: Approve capped default with opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the 1024 default only if the PR also documents and validates an explicit way to preserve Docker-default behavior, adds tests, and includes real Docker proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox/config history and PR 102044 metadata make this the best visible individual routing candidate for the default-change decision.
